source_text:
ὅθεν οὐ μάχεται τὸ »Ὁ λαβὼν αὐτοῦ τὴν μαρτυρίαν« τῷ μηδένα αὐτὴν εἰληφέναι, τῷ ἑτέρως μὲν μὴ λαμβάνεσθαι αὐτήν, * * * οἳ καὶ ἐκ τοῦ εἰληφέναι τὴν Ἰησοῦ μαρτυρίαν σφραγίζουσι καταθέσει βεβαίᾳ τὸν θεὸν ἀληθῆ εἶναι, μαθόντε
Ὅτι] Τὸ »Ἓν« πολλαχῶς λέγεται καὶ καθ’ ὁμοιότητα καὶ καθ’ ἕτερα πολλά· καὶ κατὰ μὲν συμφωνίαν, ὅταν εἴπῃ ὅτι »Τὸ πλῆθος τῶν πιστευσάντων ἦν ἡ καρδία μία καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ μία«, καθ’ ὁμοιότητα δέ, ὡς ὅταν λέγῃ· »Καὶ γὰρ ἡμεῖς πάντες έν ἑνὶ πνεύματι εἰς ἓν σῶμα ἐβαπτίσθημεν‘ καθ᾿ ὁμοιότητα τῆς φύσεως· καὶ ὡς τὸν Ἀδὰμ ἀρχὴν καὶ κεφαλὴν ἔχοντες κατὰ φύσιν ἡμῶν γεννήσεως ἓν σῶμα λεγόμεθα οἱ πάντες ἔχειν, οὕτως καὶ τὸν χριστὸν κεφαλὴν ἐπιγραφόμεθα διὰ τῆς θείας ἀνγεννήσεως ἥτις γέγονε τύπος ἡμῖν τοῦ θανάτου καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτοῦ, ὃς πρωτότοκος ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστάς. ἐπιγραφόμεθα αὐτὸν κεφαλὴν κατὰ προτύπωσιν τῆς αὐτοῦ ἀναστάσεως »οὐτινος ἐσμὲν μέλη ἐκ μέρους καὶ σῶμα διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος »εἰς ἀφθαρσίαν ἀναγεννώμενοι«.
thought_title: Receiving Jesus' testimony and the unity of believers
orientation: Origen is resolving the apparent contradiction in John 3:32-33 between no one receiving Jesus' testimony and some receiving it, then explaining the many senses of 'one' in Scripture.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the saying "He who received his testimony" does not conflict with no one having received it, because in one way it is not received, * * * who also from having received the testimony of Jesus seal with a firm deposit that God is true, having learned. [Lemma:] The word "One" is said in many ways, both according to likeness and according to many other things; and according to agreement, when it says that "The multitude of those who believed had one heart and one soul"; according to likeness, as when it says: "For we all were baptized in one Spirit into one body," according to likeness of nature; and just as having Adam as beginning and head according to the nature of our birth we are all said to have one body, so also we inscribe Christ as head through the divine regeneration which has become a type for us of his death and resurrection, who rose as firstborn from the dead. We inscribe him as head according to the prefiguration of his resurrection, "of whom we are members in part and body through the Spirit," being regenerated into incorruption.

choices.why: κατάθεσις is a deposit or pledge; βεβαίᾳ means firm or secure. The phrase describes the act of sealing God's truth as a secure pledge.
ἐπιγράφω means to write upon or inscribe; here it is used metaphorically of taking Christ as head, as one would inscribe a name or title.
The form is a variant spelling of ἀναγέννησις, meaning regeneration or rebirth, the divine new birth through baptism.
προτύπωσις means a prefiguring or type; it refers to Christ's resurrection as a pattern or type for believers.

bible_refs.note: Τὸ πλῆθος τῶν πιστευσάντων ἦν ἡ καρδία μία καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ μία
Καὶ γὰρ ἡμεῖς πάντες έν ἑνὶ πνεύματι εἰς ἓν σῶμα ἐβαπτίσθημεν
οὐτινος ἐσμὲν μέλη ἐκ μέρους καὶ σῶμα διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος

pass_b_english: So there is no contradiction between "the one who receives his testimony" and the statement that no one has received it, because it is received in one way and not in another. Those who have received Jesus' testimony set their seal with firm assent that God is true, having learned [the text breaks off here].

The word "one" is used in many ways, both according to likeness and according to many other things. It is used according to agreement, as when Scripture says, "The multitude of those who believed had one heart and one soul" (Acts 4:32). It is used according to likeness, as when it says, "For we were all baptized in one Spirit into one body" (1 Corinthians 12:13), according to likeness of nature. And just as we all, having Adam as our beginning and head according to the nature of our birth, are said to have one body, so also we inscribe Christ as our head through the divine regeneration, which has become for us a type of his death and resurrection. He rose as firstborn from the dead. We inscribe him as head according to the prefiguration of his resurrection, "of whom we are members in part and a body through the Spirit," being regenerated into incorruption [the text is corrupt here].
notes: The source text contains a lacuna marked by * * * after 'μὴ λαμβάνεσθαι αὐτήν', where text is missing. The gloss reflects only what is present.
The form 'ἀνγεννήσεως' appears to be a variant or misspelling of 'ἀναγεννήσεως' (regeneration).
The form 'έν' in 'έν ἑνὶ πνεύματι' appears to be a typographical variant of 'ἐν'.
The form 'οὐτινος' appears to be a variant of 'οὗτινος' (of whom).

problems.quote: seal with a firm deposit that God is true
problems.source_quote: σφραγίζουσι καταθέσει βεβαίᾳ τὸν θεὸν ἀληθῆ εἶναι
problems.why: Here κατάθεσις means assent or affirmation, not a deposit. 'Firm deposit' is a misleading dictionary gloss that makes the clause hard to follow.
problems.fix: Those who have received Jesus' testimony set their seal, with firm assent, that God is true
problems.ruling: κατάθεσις here is firm assent/affirmation; “firm deposit” misleads how σφραγίζουσι τὸν θεὸν ἀληθῆ εἶναι.

last_rejected.why: Source has 'when he/it says' without specifying Scripture; English adds 'Scripture says' which attributes words to Scripture, but this is Origen's voice quoting, not marked as Scripture in source. Actually this is minor. The 'he' could refer to Scripture personified or an author. But 'Scripture says' is an interpretive addition.
last_rejected.ruling: ‘ὅταν εἴπῃ’ = ‘when he/it says’; adding ‘Scripture says’ is a clarifying gloss, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: 'ἐκ μέρους' means 'individually' or 'severally' (each member), not 'in part' (partially). This changes Paul's meaning about individual members forming one body.
last_rejected.ruling: ‘ἐκ μέρους’ can mean ‘from a part/each part’; ‘in part’ is a permissible rendering, not a substantive error.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes γέννησις as 'birth', banned 'generation'. 'Regeneration' contains 'generation' and translates ἀναγέννησις/rebirth context, but the core term γέννησις must be 'birth'. The related word should use 'rebirth' to maintain consistency.
last_rejected.ruling: ‘ἀνγεννήσεως’ = ‘regeneration, rebirth’; translation matches lexical meaning, no glossary breach.

last_rejected.why: Same issue: ἀναγεννώμενοι should use 'rebirth' root, not 'regeneration' with banned 'generation'.
last_rejected.ruling: ‘ἀναγεννώμενοι’ = ‘being regenerated’; translation is accurate and consistent with the term.
